transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining the pre-publication check-in for 'Glass Harbor.' Before we finalize the catalog, I need to hear from submissions and technical screening staff on two things: first, the premiere status of the film, which is still marked for confirmation, and second, whether there are any issues with the master file. As you know, the catalog draft currently lists the film at 94 minutes, which would exceed the 90-minute limit for national competition. So depending on what we learn today, we may need to confirm whether Glass Harbor is placed in the national competition or moved to the panorama program. Please go ahead and share any status or master-file issues you're aware of.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I checked the national festival database yesterday and confirmed that 'Glass Harbor' already had a public screening at the Coastline Film Week in this country. I recorded the result in my local review notes, but the database export feeding Mara's catalog review has not yet refreshed, so it may not be visible in the current catalog data.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I completed ingest quality control this morning and confirmed that the filmmaker's approved festival cut is an 88-minute DCP, not the 94-minute listed in the catalog draft. The QC report is waiting in the technical queue and hasn't yet been attached to the programming record.
transcript.speaker: A3

decisions.catalog_premiere_status: not a national premiere (previously screened at Coastline Film Week)

commitments.detail: Update the runtime from 94 minutes to 88 minutes to match the approved festival cut DCP.
Update premiere status to reflect that Glass Harbor is not a national premiere due to its prior screening at Coastline Film Week.
Confirm placement of Glass Harbor in the panorama program, as it is not eligible for national competition.
Attach the QC report for the 88-minute DCP to the programming record.
Refresh the database export so the premiere status is visible in catalog review data going forward.
